clue.text: Heading off criticism by community, old cleaner's using lots of water

indicators.note: the head of the word for criticism is cut off, losing its first letter

parts.note: flak is hostile criticism
EC is the European Community
Omo is an old brand of washing powder

explanation.surface: A grumble about a community's old washing powder and how much water it wastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' trims FLAK to LAK. The lake is in northern Italy, beside the town of Como.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian lake is, loosely, a large body of water, so a cryptic hint suits it.

clue.text: Captain may bear this mark in red, leaving scene

indicators.note: the currency letter is put inside the trimmed colour word
the abbreviation for scene departs from the colour word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A sports captain's badge being described as a mark in red after he left the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' strips the scene abbreviation from the colour word, and 'in' sets the currency letter inside what remains. A team captain traditionally wears a band on the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket captain wears an armband, a decorative band round the upper arm.

clue.text: Underwear that's hot or cold on cobblers

parts.note: a sink has a hot tap and a cold tap
British slang: cobblers and pants both mean rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone asking which underwear suits a heatwave or a cold snap, while shoemakers look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, as is 'pants'. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap pants are loose, short knickers of the kind once worn under skirts for dancing.

clue.text: Gamble on a version being tested

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Putting money on a piece of software still in its trial release.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta release is the trial issue of software given to testers before launch.

clue.text: Hostile peak disrupts extremists in cartography

indicators.note: the peak breaks into the pair of letters and splits them apart
the extreme letters, first and last, of the map-making word

parts.note: a hill is a peak

explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists in' gives C and Y, the ends of cartography; 'disrupts' puts HILL between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly reception is a cold, unfriendly one, so the word extends to hostility.

clue.text: Female politician and king visit lake, then another

indicators.note: the king goes into the lake word as a visitor goes into a place

parts.note: a mere is a lake
K is the chess abbreviation for king
another lake, abbreviated as L

explanation.surface: A woman politician and a monarch touring one lake after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visit' puts K inside MERE; 'another' means a second lake, this time abbreviated L.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela Merkel was the German chancellor, a leading woman in politics.

clue.text: A tie made in 8 or 10? Some days one is in fashion

parts.note: March, abbreviated Mar, is a run of days in the year

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wedding season note: on some days a marriage is all the rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 and 10 are the answers HEAVEN and HELL: a match is said to be made in heaven, or in hell for a bad one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is a tie between two people, and the saying holds good matches are made in heaven.

clue.text: Woman describes hail in the sky

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the woman word goes round the greeting

parts.note: hen is a slang word for a woman
ave is the Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A woman giving an account of a hailstorm up above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, often plural, is a poetic word for the sky or firmament.

clue.text: Small rodents earlier destroying odd bits of curtains

parts.note: ago means in the past, earlier

explanation.surface: Little rodents having previously chewed holes in the curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the odd letters C, R, A, N of curtains leaves UTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a South American burrowing rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Governor taking sides in local underworld

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor

indicators.note: the two sides of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A governor siding with one faction in a local underworld of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A governor is addressed as His Excellency, shortened HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld of myth is the realm of the dead, the place of damnation.

clue.text: Pulse taken with both hands — a perfect example

parts.note: a pea is a pulse, an edible seed
R and L, for right and left hand

explanation.surface: A doctor taking a pulse with both hands as a model of the technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called a gem or jewel of its kind is a finest specimen, as in 'a pearl of wisdom'.

clue.text: Wood of all kinds initially seen

indicators.note: the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A note that timber of every sort is to be seen first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak is a hard timber from the tree of that name.

clue.text: Old golfer ridiculous wearing fleece

indicators.note: the con word wears the ridiculous word, holding it inside

parts.note: to fleece is to con
OTT, over the top, means ridiculous

explanation.surface: A veteran golfer looking silly in a fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a garment but is the verb meaning to swindle. Henry Cotton was a British golfer who won the Open three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Cotton was a three-time Open champion golfer of the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: It's very clear blubber adversely affected back muscles?

parts.note: to blubber is to cry

parts.note: lats are the latissimus dorsi muscles of the back

explanation.surface: Clearly someone has been crying after hurting their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adversely affected' reverses LATS to STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal glass is perfectly transparent, as in 'crystal clear'.

clue.text: Convicted druggies primarily, given a long time inside, are this?

definitions.text: Convicted druggies primarily, given a long time inside, are this?

indicators.note: the long time sits between the two initial letters
the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Convicted drug users handed a long sentence end up locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives C and D; 'inside' puts AGE between them. Read whole, the clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners serving a long term are shut away like animals behind bars.

clue.text: Lord concealing lost riches

indicators.note: the deity word hides the lost letter inside it

parts.note: the Lord is God
L stands for lost in results tables

explanation.surface: A nobleman hiding the fortune he had lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold stands for wealth, as in streets paved with it.

clue.text: Composed play with words rejected by director, being crude

parts.note: raw means crude, unrefined

indicators.note: the pun is thrown back, read from the end

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A director binning a crude, wordy play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the wordplay joke backwards; 'by' means the director's letter sits beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract or plan that is drawn up has been drafted, set down in writing.

clue.text: Entrepreneur's Italian sauces withdrawn

indicators.note: drawn back, so the sauce word reads in reverse

parts.note: ragus are Italian meat sauces

explanation.surface: A businessman taking his Italian sauces off the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sugar is a British businessman known from TV's The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Sugar, founder of Amstrad, is a famous British business tycoon.

clue.text: Part of plant, taken from Home Counties meadow, up for grabs

indicators.note: the rearranged letters seize the next pieces and hold them inside
stirred up, so the letters of 'for' are rearranged

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, where the Home Counties lie round London
a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: A bit of a plant from a meadow in the Home Counties that anyone may take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges 'for' into ROF, and 'grabs' holds the other pieces inside it. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of a rose bush is one part of the plant.

clue.text: Cook perhaps seasoning

explanation.surface: A chef adding a bit of seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef but is Captain James Cook, the navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Old seamen are nicknamed salts; sodium chloride is the basic table seasoning.

clue.text: Lounge party hosted that is public

indicators.note: the party takes in 'that is' as a host takes in guests

parts.note: Lab is the Labour Party
i.e., id est, means that is
out means known to the public

explanation.surface: A lounge where a party was held, open to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab is the usual short form of Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to loaf idly, the same as lazing around.

clue.text: Acted outside in the morning with acceptable suit

indicators.note: the acted word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: did means acted
a.m. means in the morning
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: An actor performing in the morning in a decent outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Type of business lifting atmosphere around Connecticut

indicators.note: in a down light the letters are raised, so they read upwards
the mood word goes round the state abbreviation

parts.note: mood is atmosphere
CT is the postal code for Connecticut

explanation.surface: A company cheering up the mood around Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes MOCTOD; 'lifting' then turns the whole of it upwards, as suits a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet-based company is called by the name of its web address ending.

clue.text: With constant skill, perhaps steer agricultural vehicle

parts.note: a steer is a bullock, an example of an ox
c is the symbol for the speed of light, a constant
art means skill

explanation.surface: Steering a farm vehicle skilfully and steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' looks like a verb about driving but is a young bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm wagon drawn by a beast of burden serves on the land.

clue.text: Scrap with a couple about money

parts.note: a sliver is a scrap

explanation.surface: Two people fighting over cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a couple about' swaps the second and third letters of SLIVER, the L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins were once made of the precious metal, so it means cash in coins.

clue.text: Linesman perhaps havin' a game

larking about with the g dropped, like the clue's own

clue.text: Provider of seed beginning to relate to parrot

parts.note: to parrot is to ape, copy

clue.text: Woman's the latest in infirmary after stroke

indicators.note: the final letter of the hospital word

C is the tap marking for cold

clue.text: Short quiz contains language element

indicators.note: the trimmed quiz word holds the language inside it
cut short, so the quiz word loses its last letter

Latin is a language
